title: Transient per-row UPDATE error (deadlock/timeout/connection drop) now terminalises a row r1 would have re-tried
detail: The comment's premise — a per-row UPDATE error is poison data — is false for deadlock (40P01), statement_timeout (57014), lock_timeout (55P03) and post-commit connection drops: all hit the UPDATE (not the due-SELECT), all transient. r1 re-tried via StoodDown; r2 marks the row failed on the first blip.
recommended_fix: Branch on SQLSTATE in query_error: re-arm (StoodDown) for transient codes 40P01/40001/57014/55P03/08xxx, mark_failed only for poison/integrity codes (23xxx). Or count consecutive stand-downs and terminalise only after N.

title: mark_failed WHERE omits attempt_count, so a committed-but-errored advance can be clobbered to failed
location: server/src/reference_checks/sql/sweep_mark_failed.sql:18-20 (contrast sweep_advance.sql:24, sweep_claim_t0.sql:31, sweep_terminal.sql:32 which all pin attempt_count)
evidence:
WHERE id = $1
  AND status IN ('queued', 'contact_initiated')
RETURNING id::text;
-- sweep_advance.sql:24:  AND attempt_count = $4   (claim_t0: = 0; terminal: = 4)
detail: If an advance commits but returns a transport Error (connection drop after commit, before result read), the row is now status='contact_initiated' at attempt_count N+1. mark_failed (called from the Error branch) still matches and sets it failed — killing a row that already advanced.
recommended_fix: Pass the pre-advance attempt_count into mark_failed and add AND attempt_count = $3 to sweep_mark_failed.sql, mirroring the advance queries' guard so a committed advance cannot be clobbered.
